article_title_en: Best Catfish Feed Recommendations for Rapid Growth: A Phase-by-Phase Guide with FCR Targets
parity_check: ok — both ID and EN drafts contain 3 matching {IMAGE_NN} placeholders at identical positions: IMAGE_01 after lead paragraph, IMAGE_02 after phase table section, IMAGE_03 after BSF/fermentation section

images.concept: Catfish feed pellets in graduated granule sizes (0.6 mm to 4 mm) arranged by growth phase on a wooden surface
images.prompt: High-resolution close-up product photograph of African catfish (Clarias gariepinus) floating pellets arranged in four distinct clusters on a weathered teak wood surface, each cluster progressively larger in granule diameter from left to right: fine crumbles approximately 0.6-1 mm (fry phase), small round pellets approximately 1-2 mm (fingerling phase), medium round pellets approximately 2-3 mm (grow-out phase), and larger pellets approximately 3-4 mm (finisher phase). Pellets are warm amber-brown and orange-brown in color with a slightly rough matte surface texture typical of extruded aquaculture feed. Soft natural directional light from upper left casts gentle shadows that highlight pellet texture and size differences. Clean shallow depth of field keeps all four clusters in sharp focus. Background is the same warm teak wood surface, slightly defocused at the edges. No packaging, no brand text, no labels visible on the pellets themselves. Shot from a 45-degree overhead angle. Aquaculture trade publication product photography style, photorealistic, 16:9 aspect ratio, no text overlays, no watermarks, no logos, no signatures, no artificial labels or tags placed near the clusters.
images.alt_id: Pelet ikan lele empat ukuran granul (0,6 mm hingga 4 mm) tersusun di permukaan kayu sesuai fase budidaya
images.alt_en: Catfish feed pellets in four graduated granule sizes from 0.6 mm to 4 mm arranged on a wooden surface by phase
images.caption_id: Ukuran granul pelet lele harus menyesuaikan bukaan mulut di setiap fase: 0,6–1 mm untuk larva, 1–2 mm untuk pendederan, 2–3 mm untuk grower, dan 3–4 mm untuk finisher menjelang panen.
images.caption_en: Pellet granule size must match mouth gape at each phase: 0.6–1 mm for fry, 1–2 mm for fingerling, 2–3 mm for grow-out, and 3–4 mm for the finisher stage ahead of harvest.

images.concept: Vertical infographic of catfish feed phases with protein, pellet size, feeding rate, and duration columns — language-neutral icon-based design
images.prompt: Clean modern flat-design infographic illustration showing a four-phase catfish aquaculture growth timeline as four horizontal cards stacked vertically on a white background. Each card has rounded corners and a distinct soft pastel color progressing top to bottom: light sky-blue (phase 1 fry), soft mint-green (phase 2 fingerling), warm teal (phase 3 grow-out), and rich deep green (phase 4 finisher). Each card contains only language-neutral pictographic icons with no written text or numbers: a small catfish silhouette icon that grows progressively larger from the top card to the bottom card, a circular dial icon representing protein percentage, a ruler or pellet-diameter bracket icon, a clock icon representing feeding frequency, and a small calendar icon representing phase duration in days. A vertical timeline ribbon with circular nodes runs down the left side connecting all four cards. At the bottom a highlighted summary card in deep aquaculture blue contains a stack of three feed-sack icons. Generous whitespace, subtle drop shadows, professional editorial illustration style suitable for an aquaculture trade magazine. No text, no numbers, no letters, no labels rendered inside the image. 16:9 aspect ratio, white background, no watermarks, no logos.
images.alt_id: Infografik empat fase budidaya lele dengan ikon ukuran ikan, protein, ukuran pelet, dan durasi per fase
images.alt_en: Four-phase catfish feed infographic with fish-size, protein, pellet-size, and duration icons per growth phase
images.caption_id: Visualisasi empat fase pakan lele dari larva hingga finisher: protein diturunkan bertahap dari 38–40% di fase benih ke 28–32% menjelang panen, sementara ukuran granul naik dari 0,6 mm ke 4 mm mengikuti pertumbuhan ikan.
images.caption_en: Four-phase catfish feed visualization from fry to finisher: crude protein drops gradually from 38–40 percent at the fry stage to 28–32 percent pre-harvest, while pellet granule size climbs from 0.6 mm to 4 mm in step with fish growth.
images.fallback_note: Editor QC (2026-05-26): generated infographic rendered the phase labels and side-text as garbled glyphs (e.g. 'Caatiulture Afdesh Tinelin', 'Wolle- 3 Grow-Out', 'Phase 2 Fingerling' partially legible). FLUX failed to produce legible label text as predicted. RECOMMENDATION before publish: replace with a designer-built SVG chart, a Canva/Figma export, or a clean stock infographic. The article body table carries all precise data and is canonical.

images.concept: Realistic Indonesian catfish pond at midday with catfish surfacing for floating pellets, healthy green water, farmer at pond edge with feed bucket
images.prompt: Editorial documentary photograph of an Indonesian catfish aquaculture farmer in his late 30s wearing a plain light-blue cotton long-sleeve shirt and dark work trousers with no visible brand logos, standing at the edge of a rectangular open-top earthen or tarpaulin-lined catfish pond in rural Java or Sumatra during midday. He is holding a simple plastic bucket in one outstretched hand, caught in the motion of scattering floating pellets across the water surface. The pond surface shows dozens of dark grey-brown African catfish (Clarias gariepinus) vigorously surfacing and competing for the floating pellets, creating splashing and rippling. The pond water is a healthy jade-green color from phytoplankton bloom, indicating good water quality. The background shows lush tropical vegetation, a glimpse of simple farm infrastructure such as a low wooden or bamboo fence, and soft blue-white sky. Bright midday Indonesian sunlight, high-key natural exposure, clear sharp focus on the catfish surfacing at the feed area and on the farmer's hand releasing pellets. Full-frame photographic style, 50mm equivalent, photorealistic, authentic working farm documentary atmosphere, not staged or commercial looking. No text overlays, no brand labels, no watermarks, no logos, no signatures. 16:9 aspect ratio.
images.alt_id: Pembudidaya Indonesia menaburkan pelet apung di kolam lele, puluhan lele berebut makan di permukaan air hijau
images.alt_en: Indonesian catfish farmer scattering floating pellets over a pond, dozens of catfish surfacing to feed in green-tinted water
images.caption_id: Pelet apung memungkinkan metode satiation feeding: pembudidaya bisa langsung melihat kapan lele berhenti menyambar dan menghentikan pemberian sebelum ada sisa pakan yang mencemari dasar kolam.
images.caption_en: Floating pellets enable the satiation feeding method: the farmer can see exactly when catfish stop striking the surface and halt feeding before uneaten residue reaches the pond floor.
images.fallback_note: Editor QC (2026-05-26): generated image looks acceptable. Catfish anatomy reads correctly (visible barbels and dark body coloration). One minor framing deviation: the farmer is rendered standing inside the pond rather than at the edge as the prompt requested. Still passes for editorial use; if a fully cropped 'at-edge' framing is needed for a hero placement, a stock photo would be a clean fallback.

notes: All three prompts deliberately avoid rendered text, numbers, or labels inside the image — FLUX text rendering at this resolution is unreliable and all data is already in the article body tables.
Same image set is shared between pakan-ikan-lele-01.id.docx and pakan-ikan-lele-01.en.docx. Only alt_id/alt_en and caption_id/caption_en differ between language versions.

IMAGE_02 infographic is icon-only by design. If the editor or client requires a true annotated table visual with legible numbers (protein %, feeding rate figures), this should be commissioned as a designed asset rather than AI-generated.

IMAGE_03 catfish anatomy note: Clarias gariepinus has a distinctive flat broad head and long barbels. Post-generation QC should verify FLUX did not render a generic tilapia-like fish silhouette instead.

No STP product packaging requested or attempted — brand-specific packaging mockups are flagged as hard/unreliable for FLUX. The pellets in IMAGE_01 are generic unbranded aquaculture feed, appropriate for the article's educational (not product-ad) framing.
